page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-highmem-4-lssd is an Arm-based virtual machine configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs and 32 GB of memory, yielding an 8 GB per vCPU ratio. Powered by 3.0 GHz Arm Neoverse-V2 cores based on the ARMv8 architecture, the instance incorporates 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 80 MB of shared L3 cache, backed by hardware-accelerated AES cryptography instructions. It includes a dedicated 402 GB NVMe local solid-state drive for high-speed scratch space or low-latency local persistence, without bundled graphics processing units.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong memory and compression throughput. The instance achieves a top-quartile PassMark memory score of 2,910.05 and single-threaded gzip compression throughput of 32.26 GB/sec, alongside large-block memory read bandwidth of 102.77 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 36.96 GB/sec. General multi-core processing performance remains in the middle tier, yielding a Geekbench multi-core score of 6,386.0 and stress-ng multi-core metric of 7,256.38. Conversely, synthetic compute tests reveal lower ratings in PassMark extended instructions and encryption, while larger language model inference shows diminished prompt and generation rates due to the absence of hardware accelerators.

With its 8:1 memory-to-vCPU allocation and bundled NVMe local storage, the instance provides high resource density for memory-bound tasks without requiring high vCPU overhead. It operates efficiently for in-memory caching layers such as Redis, relational and non-relational database nodes, software compilation pipelines, and transactional web serving where dedicated low-latency local storage is required.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4a-highmem-4-lssd is a general-purpose, memory-dense virtual machine featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs on the 3.0 GHz Arm Neoverse-V2 architecture and 32 GB of RAM, offering an 8 GB per vCPU footprint. The system includes 402 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and hardware AES support, but does not provide GPU accelerators. In synthetic and application benchmarks, the instance demonstrates high performance in memory subsystems, scoring 2,910.05 in PassMark memory and delivering 32.26 GB/sec in gzip compression, alongside moderate mid-tier CPU and caching metrics such as 8.56 million Redis SET operations per second and 10.76 GB/sec static web serving throughput. Compute-bound tasks without specialized Arm vector extensions represent clear performance boundaries. c4a-highmem-4-lssd is suitable for memory-intensive caching, medium database workloads, continuous integration build jobs, and I/O-sensitive application serving.
